insight: During the match between Belgium and Iran, the hydration breaks seemed to have a more significant impact on Belgium's attacking momentum, as they experienced a decrease in actions per minute after both breaks, with a change of -0.20/min, indicating a slight loss of momentum. In contrast, Iran's attacking momentum was less affected, with no change after the first break and a smaller decrease of -0.10/min after the second break, suggesting they were able to maintain their rhythm better. Overall, Iran appears to have benefited more from the hydration breaks, as they were able to capitalize on Belgium's loss of momentum, particularly after the second break when they outperformed Belgium 2-1 in terms of actions. This shift in momentum may have contributed to Iran's ability to stay competitive in the match, despite Belgium's initial strong start.
